evidence: paper: \nabla_* f = (D_r f,\, D_\theta f,\, D_z f), \qquad \operatorname{div}_* a = (D_r + R^{-1}) a_r + D_\theta a_\theta + D_z a_z, \qquad \operatorname{curl}_* a = \big( D_\theta a_z - D_z a_\theta,\; D_z a_r - D_r a_z,\; (D_r + R^{-1}) a_\theta - D_\theta a_r \big).

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. All three operators appear, but as separate definitions in three files rather than as one display, and with D_θ written out as R⁻¹ times a bare angular derivative instead of as the single symbol D_θ = R^{-1}∂_θ of the line above (3.11). Component by component: HarmonicCalculus.cylindricalDivergence is (D_r + R^{-1})a_r + D_θ a_θ + D_z a_z with D_r = along Vr, D_θ = (R)⁻¹ • along Vθ, D_z = along Vz; CurlClassBounds.cylindricalCurl has exactly the paper's three curl components in the same order and with the same signs, including the connection term (R)⁻¹ • a 1 in the axial component; CurlGeometry.cylindricalCurl / cylindricalDiv are the same two formulas in a purely algebraic form over a commutative ring with q standing for R^{-1} and Dθ for ∂_θ. For ∇_*, LinearWaveResidual.gradient is exactly the paper's triple for a plain scalar p : E → ℂ, in the same frame idiom (along Vr/Vθ/Vz, R) as the divergence and curl above, with D_θ = R⁻¹ along Vθ; LiftedMeanResidual.realGradient is the same body for a real scalar, with * for •. LinearWaveResidual.gradient is consumed at LinearWaveResidual.lean:60 inside linearResidual, in the pressure-gradient slot of the momentum residual, i.e. it is the ∇_* the later argument uses. HarmonicResidual.gradient is a weaker variant of the same formula, in the coefficient algebra of a normalized graph (oscillatory factor stripped, angular dependence carried by the harmonic index kp) rather than on a plain scalar. The Lean operators act through frame direction fields Vr, Vθ, Vz rather than through the paper's explicitly √Q-scaled D_r, D_z.
